sections.h2: What does the Catawba County Register of Deeds record?
sections.html:
The Catawba County Register of Deeds records and keeps deeds, deeds of trust, satisfactions, powers of attorney, plats, easements, rights of way, assumed names and similar land documents. It also holds birth and death records, issues marriage licenses and administers notary oaths. Land records run from 1842, when Lincoln County gave up the territory that became Catawba County, and anything earlier is in Lincoln County.

The office takes documents for recording and lets the public view filed records Monday to Friday, 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., except holidays. Its phone number is (828) 465-1573. Indexes and images go online once a document is recorded, with the caution that they have not been verified. The county says recorded documents are scanned within one business day.

The register is elected, and by state law the office cannot draft documents or give legal advice. If you need a deed prepared, hire a North Carolina attorney. For wills and divorces, the clerk of superior court is the right office, reachable at (828) 695-6100.

sections.h2: How do you record a deed in Catawba County?
sections.html:
You bring or send the signed and acknowledged deed with the right fees, or you submit it electronically through an approved provider. Catawba County accepts all document types for eRecording and names two providers: Simplifile at 800-460-5657 and CSC at 866-652-0111. A submitter first completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider. The county reports that 16,868 real estate documents were eRecorded in 2023, about 74 percent of the total.

Paper filers should check a short list before the trip:

  • Every deed must show the grantee's current mailing address before it can be recorded.
  • Every map or real estate instrument needs the name and address of the person it should be returned to.
  • Documents to be mailed back need a self-addressed stamped envelope of the right size.
  • The instrument must meet the state's recording standards, and the office says it uses Times New Roman as its standard font.
  • A cover sheet may be required for some documents, so ask first if you are unsure.

Recording order matters. Under G.S. 47-18, a conveyance is not valid against lien creditors or purchasers for value until it is registered in the county where the land lies, and priority follows the order of registration by time. Ask your closing attorney when the deed will reach the register.

sections.h2: What do recording fees and the deed excise tax cost in Catawba County?
sections.html:
Recording fees are set by state statute and the county adds a few surcharges that show up in its own fee notes. The excise tax is separate, and the seller pays it. The table collects the figures as printed by the county and by G.S. 161-10.

Catawba County recording charges as printed in the county notes and state statute
ItemAs printedSource
Ordinary instrument$26.00 first 15 pages, $4.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Deed of trust or mortgage$64.00 first 35 pages, $4.00 each added pageG.S. 161-10
Plat recorded$21.00 per sheetG.S. 161-10
Nonstandard document$25.00 added feeCounty recording fees page; G.S. 161-10(a)(18a)
Assignment referencing extra deeds of trust$10 for each reference beyond the firstCounty recording fees page
More than 20 parties to be indexed$2 per party addedCounty recording fees page
Copy of a recorded deed$.25 per pageCounty how-do-I page
Copy of a recorded plat$2.00County how-do-I page
Excise tax on conveyance$1.00 per $500 of consideration or fractionG.S. 105-228.30

The county explains the excise tax as $2.00 per $1,000 of the purchase price, paid by the grantor or seller, and notes that no stamp applies when no consideration changed hands. Satisfactions of deeds of trust are recorded without a fee. The office accepts cash, business checks and debit or credit cards.

The excise tax is collected before the deed is recorded. The statute splits it: half to the county general fund and half, less refunds and an allowance, to the state.

sections.h2: Where do you look up a Catawba County property by address?
sections.html:
The register's records describe land by legal description, not by street address, so an address search belongs with Tax Mapping. Call (828) 465-8420 or use the county's online real estate maps, keeping in mind that the GIS map is not a legal or binding map. Then take the parcel details to the Register of Deeds online deed search to read the chain of title.

The office notes that it cannot correct a missing item, error or misspelling on an original recorded document under G.S. 132-3, so ask the office what it can do and expect to need an attorney for a correction. If a deed is lost, the office can issue a certified copy bearing its seal, which carries the same weight as the original.

The office also reminds the public that the primary evidence of ownership of land is the recording of the deed, not the paper itself. Sellers who inherited a house or bought it long ago should check that the vesting deed appears in the index before listing.

sections.h2: How does recording tie to selling a Catawba County house?
sections.html:
Closing in Catawba County ends with three recordings: the deed to the buyer, the buyer's deed of trust if financed, and satisfaction of the seller's old loan. The satisfaction carries no recording fee. Contracts to convey, options and leases over three years must also be registered to bind later purchasers.

The state's contract-for-deed law applies to one to four family homes where the seller keeps title for five or more payments. It requires recording of the contract or a memorandum within five business days, and a buyer may cancel through midnight of the third business day after signing. A seller who has sold on a contract for deed should confirm that the memorandum is in the Catawba County index.

Tax matters ride alongside recording. Current-year property tax is due September 1, and the Catawba County Tax Office can give a payoff figure for your parcel. Deferred circuit breaker taxes, if any, become due on transfer.

sections.h2: What is Catawba County like for a house seller?
sections.html:
Catawba County covers 413 square miles, 399 of them land, in the foothills of the Blue Ridge. Census Bureau figures put the population at 170,172 in the July 1, 2025 estimate and the number of housing units at 77,827. The 2020-2024 median value of an owner-occupied home is $241,600, and 72.2 percent of homes are occupied by their owners.

The county issued 1,944 building permits in 2025, and median household income is $67,864. A title search on an old tract can reach back past 1842, and the county says records from before that year are held in Lincoln County.

faqs.q: Where is the Catawba County Register of Deeds?
faqs.a: The county site gives real estate recording hours of 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., Monday to Friday, except holidays, and a phone line of (828) 465-1573. Ask for the office's current street address when you call. eRecording is also available.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to record a deed in Catawba County?
faqs.a: An ordinary instrument costs $26.00 for the first 15 pages plus $4.00 for each additional page under G.S. 161-10, with a $25.00 charge added if the document is nonstandard. The seller also pays the excise tax of $1.00 per $500 of the price. A deed of trust runs $64.00 for the first 35 pages.

faqs.q: Can Catawba County record a deed electronically?
faqs.a: Yes. The county accepts all document types for eRecording through Simplifile (800-460-5657) and CSC (866-652-0111). The submitter completes a memorandum of understanding with the provider first. The county counted 16,868 eRecorded real estate documents in 2023.

faqs.q: Does the Register of Deeds prepare deeds in Catawba County?
faqs.a: No. State law bars the office from preparing legal documents or giving legal advice, so you need an attorney to draft or correct a deed. The office can show you how to use the indexes and can issue certified copies of recorded deeds at $.25 per page.

faqs.q: Who pays the deed excise tax in Catawba County?
faqs.a: The seller, called the transferor or grantor, pays it to the register of deeds before the deed is recorded. The rate is $1.00 for each $500 of consideration, or fraction of $500. The county says no stamp applies when no consideration was exchanged.
